The table is importet from googlesheets with

#Load google sheet Retrieval, worksheet inputs
gs_retrieval_inputs_read<-function(){
 retrieval_sheet<-gs_key("15D7cO_Ef5g1VF4ruxFvdvyUMLpbqZEvvB8wF-lv6g_c")
 
 gs_read(retrieval_sheet,ws="inputs")
}

and the Retrieve Button executes the following store function in the same google sheet:

#Update google sheet Retrieval, worksheet inputs
gs_retrieval_inputs_store<-function(inputs){
 
  #Get the google sheet to store data in
  #Important for google sheets: Colums need to be named and one set of values needs to be inserted in a row
  retrieval_sheet<-gs_key("15D7cO_Ef5g1VF4ruxFvdvyUMLpbqZEvvB8wF-lv6g_c")
 
  #Add a new row in google sheet, specificly in worksheet ws "Sheet1" with values in input
  gs_add_row(retrieval_sheet,input = inputs,ws="inputs")
 
}

Any ideas? The error looks like it has something to do with the authentification of the google sheet, but why does it work when only reading is done? In the google sheet "File/Share..." I have "Anyone with the link can edit" chosen, so there shouldn't be the problem.

Thx a lot!

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] "Disconnected from Server" Error: oauth_listener()
parts:
I am not super familiar with oAuth, but I believe there is a way for you to essentially get an oauth token that you can bundle up with your application for it to use and not require the authentication flow.  I know there is a bug in the IDE today where deploying the application won't send up the .httr-oauth file, but you can get around that by deploying by running: rsconnect::deployApp()  

Hopefully this gives you enough hints, or maybe someone else from the forums can help.
-Tareef
